text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Jewish organisations in Netherlands call on Dutch banks to publish a list of dormant Jewish accounts. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchanges breaks through the 1000-point barrier for the first time, closes at new record 998.48. (p1)
- Software maker Baan sustains turnover growth of 65 percent in first 1997 half. (p3)
- Court upholds pig-breeding ban ordered by Dutch farm minister Jozias van Aartsen to curb swine fever. (p7)
- Merchant bank MeesPierson sheds stake in options trader Optiver. (p11)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Software giant Microsoft to recruit 1,750 staff in Netherlands to meet burgeoning Dutch market demand. (p1)
- Foods group Nutricia director Dick van Hedel to leave the company and head retail concern Groenwoudt Groep. (p2)
- Property fund Capa City agrees to takeover by sector rival Uni-Invest. (p13)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Royal Dutch/Shell's U.S. subsidiary Shell Oil books 15 pct higher Q2 net at $ 531 million. (p29)
- Wafer stepper producer ASM Lithography upbeat on 1997 H2 prospects. (p29)
- Next government must create a more favourable tax climate for family businesses, says Peter Swinkels, chairman of Dutch branch of Family Business Network FBN. (p31)
TROUW
- ING unit Postbank refuses custom of extreme right party CP '86. (p4)
- 50 biggest Dutch travel agencies see strong turnover growth this year. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Vredestein subsidiary Hevea can hardly keep up with demand for wellington boots resulting from bad weather and swine fever outbreak. (p1)
